brief_rationale: The doctor met all seven responsibility-chain items with no serious or minor errors. Red-flag screening was performed, medication safety boundaries were established, and a concrete follow-up plan with owner/timing/materials was provided. HO1 was completed: the doctor discovered the hidden context of post-operative acromegaly with octreotide therapy and glucose-tolerance abnormality through workspace queries and integrated it into the tailored plan. HO3 was completed: explicit bounded closure was provided with clear owner assignment, residual uncertainties acknowledged, and escalation criteria. No other high-order points were triggered (HO2 required a patient misconception which never appeared; HO4 was mooted by the doctor proactively clarifying the order-versus-result distinction).

high_order_assessment.explanation: Doctor discovered hidden context (post-operative GH adenoma, octreotide 30mg injection, glucose-tolerance abnormality, follow-up requirements) through workspace queries and patient clarification, and integrated these facts into a tailored follow-up checklist and safety plan.

HO2 requires a patient misconception to appear in the trajectory. The patient asked appropriate clarifying questions but never stated a false belief about IGF-1 being a diabetes test, nasal endoscopy proving tumor recurrence, octreotide being a casual anti-inflammatory, or 'no discomfort' meaning no follow-up needed.

high_order_assessment.explanation: Doctor provided explicit bounded closure: clarified what is known (IGF results, stable status), what remains unverified (formal endocrinology review, GH/IGF-1 trending), assigned owner/timing (endocrinology within 1 week of next injection), and confirmed patient receipt with red-flag escalation.

HO4 requires checking status of at least two confusing entries because patient cannot provide values. Here, the patient provided actual IGF-1/IGFBP-3 values with reference ranges, and the doctor proactively clarified the nasal endoscopy order-versus-report distinction before a false-positive/negative risk materialized.
